prompt:
A clean, straight-on photo of a printed broadside ballad sheet, headed 'THE MILL LANE BALLAD' with the small line 'Scheme: A B B A  C D D C  E F F E'. Print EXACTLY 12 numbered lines (1. to 12.) of verse, each at least SIX words long, about a mill village.

CRITICAL WRITING LAW: the rhyme scheme is enclosed -- A B B A, then C D D C, then E F F E -- and it is judged on the LAST THREE LETTERS of each line's final word. So lines 1 and 4 share an ending, lines 2 and 3 share a different one, lines 5 and 8 share a third, lines 6 and 7 a fourth, lines 9 and 12 a fifth, lines 10 and 11 a sixth. All six endings must be different from one another, and no final word may appear twice.

Deep red heading, black text, nothing else on the sheet.
easy_question: This image was supposed to show a printed sheet with numbered lines of verse. Ignoring artistic quality and ignoring whether the wording is correct, does the image DEPICT that -- a printed page or board carrying a numbered list of text lines? A photo, a scan or a clean page all count as yes. Answer NO only if it is blank, or shows something unrelated. Answer yes or no only.

reference.q_read: This image is a page carrying 12 numbered lines of text. Transcribe the 12 numbered lines EXACTLY as written, in order. Copy every word, keep the original spelling, and keep the spaces between words. If a numbered line wraps onto a second printed row, keep it as ONE line. Separate one numbered line from the next with a single pipe character | and nothing else. Do NOT transcribe the title, any heading or any word bank. Do not add commentary, line numbers or quotation marks. Output only the transcribed lines separated by |.

Copy every word letter for letter, and keep each word's capital letters and small letters exactly as they are printed. Do not fix spelling, do not change the order of the words, do not add a word and do not leave one out. Leave out the title, any sub-heading, and any text that carries no number. Write out the list and nothing else.
